disputed

/dih-SPYOO-tid/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Disputed means subject to disagreement or argument; not settled.

The tiny island has been disputed territory for decades, with two nations each producing old maps to support their claim.

Example

The umpire ruled the runner safe, but the call remained disputed for days. Slow-motion replays seemed to show the tag landing first, and players, fans, and sportswriters argued about it all week.

The call is disputed because people on both sides keep disagreeing about it and it never gets settled; the replays and week-long arguments show the question staying open. Notice that disputed describes the call itself, not the people arguing.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

contested: Contested means actively fought or argued over, with rivals pressing competing claims: a contested election, a contested will. It is the nearest neighbor of disputed and often interchangeable with it, though disputed leans on the question staying unsettled while contested stresses the active fight.

debated: Debated means argued about from different sides, usually in organized discussion, the way a policy is debated in committee. Debate is an orderly exchange of arguments and can stay perfectly friendly. Disputed is harder-edged: each side rejects the other's claim outright.

contentious: Contentious describes an issue that reliably provokes heated argument: raise it, and tempers flare. The word is about the heat an issue generates. Disputed is about the standoff itself, rival parties each asserting a claim the other side refuses to accept.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

settled: resolved and no longer argued about

accepted: agreed on by everyone

Where it sits · how heated the arguing gets

questioned → disputed → controversial

questioned vs. disputed: Questioned is milder; a questioned fact faces some doubt, but a disputed fact has people actively arguing on opposite sides.

controversial vs. disputed: Disputed is strong, but controversial goes further, suggesting heated public argument and strong emotions rather than just an unsettled question.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-: apart, in different directions

Root — put: to think, to reckon (Latin putare)

Suffix — -ed: adjective-forming ending

Put it together: Disputed builds on dis- (apart) plus the Latin root putare (to think or reckon) plus the adjective ending -ed. A disputed matter is one that people literally 'reckon apart' on: their thinking pulls in different directions and nothing is settled.

Use the root in a new word: compute: Engineers used the new software to compute the bridge's exact load limits.

Word Choice

Neutral / academic

Common collocations: a disputed call, a disputed claim, a disputed border, a disputed election. Disputed describes the thing people disagree about, never the person doing the disagreeing; the person who pushes back against an official decision dissents, and a single formal statement of opposition is an objection.
